subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should remote node-host `openclaw models auth login` fail closed before provider auth starts, or should OpenClaw support gateway-side credential forwarding for this flow?
rationale: The fix changes a provider credential boundary and determines whether node hosts may acquire and transfer gateway-owned OAuth material, which is a product/security decision rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Fail closed before auth starts
options.body: Block auth login when node-host config points at a non-loopback remote gateway and instruct the user to run auth on the gateway host.

options.title: Forward credentials to gateway
options.body: Design an authenticated gateway RPC/setup flow that stores the returned provider credential in the gateway auth store without consuming it locally first.

options.title: Warn but allow local write
options.body: Keep the current local write path with an explicit warning, accepting that users can still consume credentials on the wrong host.

recommendation.title: Fail closed before auth starts
recommendation.body: Block auth login when node-host config points at a non-loopback remote gateway and instruct the user to run auth on the gateway host.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the maintainer draft for this exact guard and already framed the fail-closed behavior and verification path.
